summary: Intro discovery for Redwood PLG path. Customer evaluating time-to-first-token for self-serve Hosted API, but interested in Dedicated/Private for data residency and latency guarantees. Discussed free credits, quickstart, security/SOC2, VPC options, benchmarking, and next steps to provision credits and run pilot benchmarks.
topics: Performance: latency SLOs, KV cache, batching
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Liam, our solutions engineer. quick intro?
[00:08] Liam: Hi all, Liam Chen here, I do infra and perf for inference.
[00:12] Rajiv: Rajiv Patel, CTO at Nimbus Fleet — thanks for squeezing us in.
[00:16] Sofia: Sofia, product. Diego  gonna chime in for ML specifics.
[00:20] Diego: Yep hi—Diego here.
[00:24] Maya: Great. Agenda: we want to run through your goals, share how Redwood's quickstart and credits get you to first token fast, then map hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private) to your requirements. Then next steps. Sound ok?
[00:36] Rajiv: Sounds perfect. Our main driver is we want to add a summarization feature into our driver ops dashboard. Small inference per request but latency matters — <~150ms tail for UI — and we also have strict data residency requirements for EU. We prefer self-serve to prototype quickly.
[00:57] Liam: Ok got it. When you say small inference, are you batching, or single-shot per request?
[01:03] Diego: Mostly single-shot, sometimes short multi-turn prompts, but usually under 512 tokens. Peak qps maybe 40-60 for some windows.
[01:11] Sofia: We also have compliance needs — customer PII cannot leave EU for certain customers.
[01:16] Maya: Understood. So two parallel tracks: quick prototyping via Hosted API with free credits and rapid TTF token, and a path to Dedicated/Private for residency and SLOs. We'll cover both.
[01:27] Liam: Quick note on cost/latency tradeoffs — for single-shot small prompts, Hosted with our low-latency zones often hits sub-200ms for many models, but Dedicated gives more predictable p99s and can be colocated in EU. Private gives full control for data residency.
[01:42] Rajiv: We saw some benchmarks online but was curious how much lift to move from Hosted to Dedicated — is it a separate contract?
[01:48] Maya: Yes Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly commit. We can start you on Hosted to prototype quickly using credits we provide, then move to Dedicated when you want predictable throughput.
[01:58] Diego: For Private, does Redwood ship an on-prem package or is it VPC-only? We need to know for our security team.
[02:05] Liam: Both options. There's a VPC deployment that keeps control plane in Redwood's region but data path in your VPC, and we also support an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements. Both integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management.
[02:18] Sofia: And SSO/SAML?
[02:20] Maya: Yes, enterprise SSO + RBAC supported. We'll share the SAML docs.
[02:25] Rajiv: Great. Can you outline the quickstart steps and how much time to first token? We need to show a demo to product leadership next week.
[02:33] Liam: For self-serve Hosted quickstart: sign up, we provision the account with trial credits (we usually start with $5k or configurable), you get API keys, SDKs (python/node), and a sample app. For a simple summarize endpoint you can get to first token in under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
[02:48] Maya: We'll send a tailored quickstart link that maps to summarization.
[02:51] Diego: 10 minutes sounds optimistic but good. Any quotas on trial credits?
[02:55] Maya: Trial limits apply but they're sufficient for an initial pilot. We can lift quotas for benchmarking — Liam can help.
[03:02] Liam: Yeah for benchmark runs we can temporarily increase rate-limits and hook into tracing so you can measure p50/p95/p99.
[03:09] Rajiv: About models — are you hosting open models or Redwood-curated ones? We need to ensure fidelity for our summarization.
[03:16] Liam: We host a catalog: curated open models and model variants optimized for latency (quantized). For higher fidelity you can pick larger variants; for cost-sensitive bursts we recommend quantized variants with minimal quality drop. We also support model rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller variants if capacity constrained.
[03:33] Sofia: You mentioned KV cache and prefix caching — is that automatic or dev-managed?
[03:38] Liam: We have automatic prefix and KV caching that can be enabled; it's workload-aware. For multi-turn chat you get big wins, for single-shot summarization it's less, but prefix caching helps if you have repeated context.
[03:47] Diego: What's the observability surface? We need token-level cost breakdowns and latency per route for our dashboards.
[03:53] Maya: Redwood Console offers per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, traces, and error analysis. We can give you access to a demo console.
[03:59] Rajiv: Security: SOC2, ISO? Log retention?
[04:03] Maya: We are SOC2 Type II and we have ISO in process — we'll include the compliance pack. Audit logs and request-level logging are available for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has standard retention but we can extend retention as an add-on.
[04:16] Sofia: For EU data residency we need keys to remain in our control. You mentioned KMS integration — can you clarify?
[04:22] Liam: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM for Private deployments. For Hosted we can support customer-managed keys via a bring-your-own-key flow in certain regions — we'll include the security note.
[04:34] Rajiv: Cost question — do you have a rough per-1k-token cost for summarization?
[04:39] Maya: Costs depend on model and quantization. For a midsize open model quantized we typically see $0.5–$2 per 1k tokens endpoint-level, but we'll send a pricing sheet with committed Dedicated rates and Hosted per-token estimates.
[04:54] Diego: For Dedicated, how long to provision a cluster and spin up a model?
[04:58] Liam: Provisioning depends on GPU availability and region — usually 3–7 days for initial provisioning once contracts are in place. Model onboarding and warmup can be done in hours; we also support continuous batching and KV cache warmup.
[05:10] Sofia: For the pilot, we want a controlled benchmark: 95th percentile under 200ms for single-shot. Is that realistic?
[05:18] Liam: With Dedicated in EU and small models it's realistic. Hosted in nearest zone may get close but Dedicated gives the margin. We'll propose a benchmark plan: test traffic pattern, synthetic replay of production calls, and compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[05:31] Rajiv: About contracts — if we like Hosted and then convert to Dedicated, is there help migrating usage and configs?
[05:38] Maya: Yes, same API and config layer across modes. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Migration is mostly configuration + capacity reservation. Our SEs help with the migration runbook.
[05:49] Diego: Any gotchas around kv cache serializations or tokenization differences across models?
[05:55] Liam: Tokenization differences exist per model family— we include tokenizer libs. KV cache serialization is handled by the runtime; if you have multi-model setups we'll discuss compatibility. We'll flag any model-specific caveats in the benchmark report.
[06:08] Sofia: Ok, can we review the timeline? We want a pilot demo to leadership 03/10.
[06:14] Maya: Timeline suggestion: 02/28 — we provision trial account + credits. 03/03 — customer shares sample workload. 03/06 — Redwood runs initial Hosted quick benchmark. 03/09 — Dedicated/private benchmarking set up, run week of 03/09. 03/10 — leadership demo with results and recommended path.
[06:31] Rajiv: That looks good. Anything else on legal/privacy?
[06:34] Maya: We'll send standard DPA template and procurement contacts. For Private/on-prem we have separate licensing terms.
[06:40] Diego: For the quickstart, can you share the sample code snippet now?
[06:43] Liam: Sure, I'll paste the Python snippet in the follow-up email. Minimal: import redwood; client = redwood.Client(api_key=...); resp = client.generate(model='rw-small-summarize', prompt=...);
[06:56] Rajiv: Perfect. Also, curious if Redwood supports function calling or structured outputs— we want JSON summary fields.
[07:03] Liam: We support structured output and function/tool calling. You can request JSON schema enforcement and Redwood will attempt to follow it; we also have evals to measure quality degradation.
[07:15] Sofia: On evals, do you offer regression alerts?
[07:18] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can monitor quality against prompt sets and raise regression alerts. We can include a starter eval for the summarization prompts.
[07:28] Rajiv: Are there known integrations with our stack— we use Kubernetes, GCP, and Kafka eventing.
[07:33] Liam: For Private we have helm charts for k8s, and for Hosted you can consume via API and push results into Kafka. We'll share integration notes for GCP VPC peering.
[07:45] Diego: Latency-wise, if we colocate Dedicated in europe-west1, what's expected p95 for rw-small?
[07:51] Liam: Ballpark p95 under 200ms for the small model with optimal batching off; p99 may be higher. We'll run benchmarks with your workload to verify.
[08:01] Sofia: Ok, important to show leadership a cost comparison. Can you send a sample TCO calc?
[08:06] Maya: We'll include a comparative TCO sheet: Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved vs Private capital/ops.
[08:13] Rajiv: Are there any limitations in the Hosted free tier around embeddings or long context lengths?
[08:19] Liam: Some very long context models have limits on free tiers, but quickstart is tuned for standard contexts. For embeddings, we have separate pricing; we'll include examples.
[08:30] Maya: Quick recap of action items before we move to Q&A — Maya will send security/compliance pack and pricing; Liam will provision test credits and a quickstart link; Diego will share sample inference workload; customer will confirm pilot timeline.
[08:45] Diego: Quick Q — for the benchmark, do you support replaying real traffic with obfuscation?
[08:50] Liam: Yes we can replay obfuscated traffic if you provide it, we also have a synthetic replay tool.
[08:56] Rajiv: Competitor question: we have teams testing Anthropic too. Any differentiation notes we should call out?
[09:02] Maya: Redwood focuses on inference serving economics and operational controls: unified runtime across deployments, observability, and cost levers like batching, quantization, KV cache. Anthropic and OpenAI have different model sets; Redwood is more vendor-agnostic and optimized for production serving and private deployments.
[09:20] Sofia: Good. Any other questions?
[09:22] Rajiv: No, that's it on my side.
[09:24] Maya: Great — we'll send the follow-ups. Thanks everyone.
[09:27] Liam: Thanks all, talk soon.
[09:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription has some small errors (names, model nicknames) — please rely on the attachments and follow-up email for canonical docs.

End of transcript.
